research_explanandum: When do owner-separated source edits preserve multiple independently maintained client obligations and when does a seemingly SOLID-inspired interface/adapter boundary improve or obstruct safe future evolution?
theoretical_hypotheses: H1: Disjoint source edit files alone are insufficient for composition when source traces share ownership-release or publication interfaces.
H2: Conditional contextual refinements compose under matching ownership transfer and frame/rely-guarantee assumptions; stale or unspecified frame assumptions invalidate any automatic gluing.

H3: If both direct and adapter architectures admit same initial client contracts, future changes touching only one implementation may favor direct; changes affecting independent consumers with different lifetime contracts may favor adapter; either preference depends on explicit admissible patches and actual observed effort, not on principle labels.
